However, this requires multiple, large doses of attenuated sporozoites, posing numerous logistical challenges. 43046913.resumo: The limited permeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is one of the key obstacles in the development of new drugs for treating brain disorders. Most small molecules fail to reach therapeutic concentrations within the brain parenchyma; this causes systemic toxicity, low efficacy, and the development of drug resistance in pathogens and tumor cells. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent a large, heterogeneous group of substances that exhibit a wide range of therapeutic effects and often show low toxicity toward healthy cells. Their ability to cross the BBB independently makes them promising drug candidates for the treatment of infectious, inflammatory, and oncological diseases of the brain. To date, only a small number of peptides are known to combine antimicrobial properties with their ability to cross the BBB. Despite the significant potential of this group of molecules, experimental data on the transport of AMPs across the BBB remain fragmentary and are often obtained using incomparable experimental conditions; moreover, some earlier findings require re-evaluation in light of current knowledge regarding the barrier function of the BBB. This review provides the first systematic compilation of scattered data on peptides that combine antimicrobial activity with the capacity for transcytosis across the BBB. Three key groups of peptides have been identified and analyzed: 1) proline-rich insect AMPs (apidaecin 137, oncocin, and drosocin); 2) endogenous mammalian neuropeptides (substance P, neuropeptide Y, vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), and pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP)); 3) cell-penetrating peptides with AMP properties (penetratin, transportan 10, pVEC). The combination of antimicrobial activity and the ability to cross BBB appears to be an achievable and reproducible characteristic for peptides of various origins, thus underlying the clear need for their discovery and development.

43043974.resumo:
Arboviruses are an increasing global public health concern, driven by both human and environmental factors. A key parameter shaping vectorial capacity for transmission is the extrinsic incubation period (EIP), the time required for a mosquito that has ingested an infectious blood meal to become capable of transmitting the virus via its saliva, which is strongly influenced by temperature. However, the temperature-EIP relationship remains poorly characterized across arboviruses and mosquito species.
We conducted the first systematic review of laboratory studies evaluating temperature effects on EIP across all reported mosquito-arbovirus pairings identifiable in the literature. We searched three databases and extracted data on infection and transmission efficiency (TE), applying a binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model to estimate the median extrinsic incubation period, the time post-infection at which 50% of infected mosquitoes become infectious.
Our synthesis included 53 studies covering 17 arboviruses. We found substantial heterogeneity in temperature effects on TE. Zika and West Nile viruses generally showed increased TE and shorter EIP at higher temperatures. However, similar trends based on published data were not clear for many viruses, such as Sindbis and chikungunya viruses, because of limited data granularity and small sample sizes. Even across different vectors of the same virus, findings varied widely, reflecting both biological differences and inconsistent experimental designs.
The findings revealed gaps in the understanding of the temperature effects on the EIP of arboviruses in mosquito vectors. Standardisation of reporting in vector competence experiments and expanded research on neglected viruses are urgently needed. Real-world environmental conditions should also be incorporated to improve modelling and support robust vector control and public health planning under changing climatic conditions.
43043974.metodo: A key parameter shaping vectorial capacity for transmission is the extrinsic incubation period (EIP), the time required for a mosquito that has ingested an infectious blood meal to become capable of transmitting the virus via its saliva, which is strongly influenced by temperature. However, the temperature-EIP relationship remains poorly characterized across arboviruses and mosquito species.

43041090.resumo: Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) is an important arbovirus in Europe. TBEV is transmitted mainly by ticks of the Ixodes ricinus (Ixodes ricinus-Ixodes persulcatus) species complex and causes infections of the central nervous system, making it one of the most important viral tick-borne diseases of humans in Europe. The natural transmission cycle relies on a complex interplay of arthropod vector and mammalian host factors. Besides the infection of ticks by feeding on viremic animals and co-feeding, transstadial transmission of the virus within the tick is also essential for further TBEV transmission to the next vertebrate host during the subsequent bloodmeal. In this study, we attempted to establish a mammalian host-tick transmission model for the simulation of the natural transmission under controlled laboratory conditions in order to study virus transmission from the reservoir host bank vole (Myodes glareolus) to I. ricinus larvae and to evaluate transstadial transmission of TBEV when engorged larvae moult into nymphs. We demonstrated acquisition of TBEV by larval ticks that blood fed on TBEV-infected viremic bank voles, although the TBEV infection prevalence of the engorged larvae was low (9.3%). Fully and partially engorged larvae were collected and further kept in the insectary and were allowed to moult into nymphs to assess transstadial virus transmission. No transstadial virus transmission was observed, as all nymphs tested negative by real-time RT-PCR. Although no general conclusions on transstadial transmission could be drawn yet, the establishment of this model forms a basis for future research.

43044838.resumo: Wolbachia is a promising new intervention for malaria control. While modelling has supported Wolbachia deployment for dengue control, its application in Anopheles is still emerging. We systematically reviewed dynamic transmission models of Wolbachia-based modified insect releases for malaria using PubMed and Embase. Evidence was compared primarily with Wolbachia-based dengue models from a parallel Wolbachia-Aedes aegypti scoping review and secondarily with gene drive-based Anopheles models identified through a separate systematic search. Across 110 included studies, three major gaps were identified. First, context-dependent fitness effects are rarely incorporated, with many models assuming high maternal transmission (MT) and cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI), limiting assessment of how environmental variability influences persistence. Second, spatial heterogeneity is infrequently modelled despite evidence that mosquito movement shapes Wolbachia spread. Third, few studies embed Wolbachia dynamics within integrated malaria transmission models, preventing estimation of epidemiological impact to assess Wolbachia's role in malaria control and elimination. Lessons from Wolbachia-based dengue control and parallel developments in gene drive provide an established framework, with actionable pathways for advancement. Addressing these priorities will be essential to guide safe, effective and scalable implementation of Wolbachia as a new malaria control intervention.

43041224.resumo: A deterministic covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI model is developed and used to gain insight into the nexus between climate and socioeconomic parameters and the transmission dynamics of dengue. The model developed a framework that incorporates two external influences: climate and socioeconomic factors. The model is rigorously analyzed, with disease-free and endemic equilibria investigated, and is simulated using data relevant to Medellín, Colombia. We then employ machine learning algorithms as an empirical feature-selection step to identify and rank socioeconomic predictors of dengue incidence, revealing that the unemployed population is the dominant socioeconomic driver. This finding motivates the selection of unemployment as the socioeconomic covariate in the mechanistic model. From our numerical simulation, we computed using temperature only and combined [temperature + socioeconomic (unemployment)] parameters to determine how their influences drive the epidemic spread. Our model suggests that socioeconomic influence can act as a driver alongside temperature, increasing the transmission rate and leading to an earlier peak. The framework is appropriate for endemic settings where socioeconomic and climatic factors are the primary drivers of transmission dynamics. The approach demonstrates how empirical machine-learning insights can inform covariate selection in mechanistic epidemiological models, thereby strengthening interpretation of how socioeconomic and climatic conditions interact to shape epidemic potential.

43045701.resumo: Defective viral genomes (DVGs) shape virus-host interactions and evolution, yet remain poorly characterized in insect-specific viruses. These DVGs retain intact terminal sequences with conserved junction motifs. A modified DRS approach reveals widespread premature termination during EILV genomic RNA synthesis, linking DVG formation to reduced replicase processivity. Notably, a subset of DVGs is selectively replicated and packaged, accumulating over serial passages and interfering with parental virus replication. Our findings uncover an intrinsic, high DVG-generating capacity in EILV, linking low-processivity RNA synthesis with increased genomic plasticity. This suggests that elevated DVG production may be an adaptive mechanism, providing important insights into alphavirus evolution and replication fidelity in insect-specific RNA viruses.

43048157.titulo: Shifting climates, shifting microbes: environmental determinants of the microbiome and impact on malaria transmission

resumo_blocos.racional: Malaria transmission dynamics are governed by complex tripartite interactions between the Anopheles mosquito, the Plasmodium parasite, and the vector's gut microbiota, all mediated by the mosquito's innate immune system. Although global malaria control is increasingly hindered by drug and insecticide resistance, significant knowledge gaps persist regarding how climate shifts and environmental variations impact vector competence.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Malaria transmission dynamics are governed by complex tripartite interactions between the Anopheles mosquito, the Plasmodium parasite, and the vector's gut microbiota, all mediated by the mosquito's innate immune system. While most experimental research relies on static laboratory conditions (typically fixed at 27 °C and 75-80% relative humidity), mosquitoes in nature experience continuous diurnal and seasonal environmental fluctuations that alter their physiology, immune responses, and microbiome.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Here, we focus on how these environmental shifts likely influence the efficacy and translational success of innovative, microbial-based control strategies, including paratransgenesis, Wolbachia-based interventions, and microbial larvicides. By examining how climate-driven variations impact both the mosquito-microbiota-parasite system and the performance of biocontrol tools, we bridge ecological and molecular perspectives to identify the current understanding of how shifting environments influence the mosquito microbiome and microbial-based tools.

10.64898/2026.11.16.767120.resumo: Dengue virus (DENV) is a major mosquito-borne human pathogen. Consistently, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated loss-of-function showed that knocking out TRIM5 or TRIM56 increases infection, while TRIM69 knockout decreases it. Restriction correlated with reduced viral RNA and viral protein levels in TRIM5- and TRIM56-expressing cells. Virus-free experiments showed that TRIM56 downregulates the DENV2 protease complex NS2B3 levels. Reciprocally, DENV2 NS2B3 reduced TRIM56 and TRIM69 abundance independently of protease activity. 10.1101/2025.10.09.681498.resumo: Viral macrodomains are promising antiviral targets that counteract host ADP-ribosylation-mediated antiviral responses in mammals. However, their role in dual-host viruses within the mosquito vector remains largely unknown. Here, we investigated the role of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) nsP3 macrodomain catalytic activity by mutating the active-site asparagine 24 (N24). Biochemical and structural analyses confirmed that these phenotypes arise in the context of a catalytically inactive macrodomain that retains ADP-ribose binding capacity, with D31 mutations lining the substrate exit path. These findings demonstrate that macrodomain catalytic activity modulates CHIKV dissemination and transmission potential in Aedes mosquitoes, revealing fundamental differences in host-dependent evolutionary advantage for a catalytically inactive viral enzyme.

Our data indicates that in CHPV infected cells, BCL-2 large splice variant expressions decreased as compared to uninfected cells. This is the first study of CHPV mediated alteration of splicing factor expressions and these results warrant further study with other viruses to better understand the global changes in host splicing events, cell survival, host immune response during virus infection.

Its immunological effects arise through several related but distinct routes. Extracellular acidosis, glucose competition, and impaired monocarboxylate transporter-dependent flux can impair CD8+ T cells, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells. Lactate- and proton-sensing receptors can also favor suppressive myeloid and regulatory-cell programs. Histone and non-histone lactylation add another layer by linking lactate availability to chromatin regulation and protein function. During sustained or repeated metabolic stress, these processes may support regulatory T-cell fitness, suppressive programs in tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, checkpoint expression, and resistance to immunotherapy. Lactylation is a plausible mediator through which sustained metabolic stress may be converted into persistent immune reprogramming; however, post-withdrawal persistence and cellular memory remain to be demonstrated in cancer. We distinguish lactate-dependent regulation from acidosis and evaluate the links to immune dysfunction and treatment resistance by their temporal, causal, and clinical support. This framework defines tests of post-exposure persistence and connects mechanistic evidence and pharmacological specificity to biomarker development and mechanism-matched trial design.

The acute phase of MI/R causes dual imbalance: excessive cardiomyocyte apoptosis and impaired macrophage phagocytosis. This pathological mechanism, the aberrant accumulation of apoptotic cells, triggers secondary necrosis, thereby serving as a critical driver of inflammatory storm and maladaptive cardiac remodeling. However, there is currently no targeted anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategy for this early pathological mechanism. Concurrently, the platform re-orchestrates cardio-immune homeostasis by cooperatively upregulating the efferocytic receptor axis (TREM2/MERTK) on macrophages via activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade. This dual coordinative effect accelerates the clearance of cellular debris and promotes the anti-inflammatory phenotypic transition from M1 to M2 macrophages, thereby attenuating the inflammatory storm, ameliorating acute-phase MI/R-induced cardiac dysfunction, and improving short-term prognosis. High-resolution spatial transcriptomics, integrated with multi-omics, confirms that MOF-Al@NVs effectively restore spatial immunometabolic homeostasis in the early infarct border zone. This biomimetic nanoplatform offers a promising strategy for targeted anti-inflammatory therapy in early MI/R injury.

We asked whether a retrospectively selected and subsequently fixed blood transcriptomic framework could relate candidate transcripts to granulocyte-associated and monocyte/macrophage-associated expression contexts rather than serve as another stand-alone diagnostic product.

Performance was examined separately across cohorts with different specimens, age groups and comparators. Transcript-score sensitivity analyses, donor-level whole-blood single-cell pseudobulk and cell-line qRT-PCR were used to assess candidate localization and cell-line expression-context concordance. Cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation were included as exploratory genetic context.
In the closest target-context cohort, GSE134347, the fixed score achieved an AUROC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.764-0.889) for sepsis versus non-infectious critical illness. Performance was lower in pediatric day-1 SIRS comparisons, indicating dependence on population and comparator context. Adjustment for alternative neutrophil-associated transcript scores produced a marker-dependent ordering, with SMPDL3A among the most attenuated and PLA2G7 among the least attenuated candidates; no candidate remained FDR-significant in the primary six-gene family. Donor-level single-cell analysis and qRT-PCR supported a monocyte/macrophage context for PLA2G7 and granulocyte-like localization of the diagnostic immune markers. Exploratory Mendelian randomisation did not support a susceptibility effect for the testable immunometabolism-associated candidates, and the HLA-DRB1 regional signal lacked evidence of a shared variant under single-variant colocalisation assumptions.
This study provides an auditable, cell-informed framework that relates granulocyte-associated transcription to PLA2G7-associated monocyte/macrophage localization within the whole-blood infection response. The framework is intended for biological prioritisation, and it defines testable candidates for future studies.

43038290.resumo: Innate immune homeostasis is vital for animal survival and requires precise control of both the intensity and duration of immune signaling. Although microRNAs (miRNAs) are known to fine-tune immune responses, their transcriptional regulation mechanisms during infection remain poorly characterized. Here, we identify an NF-κB-dependent miRNA feedback loop essential for Drosophila Toll pathway. Through dynamic expression profiling and functional genetics, we demonstrate that the NF-κB transcription factor Dif directly activates miR-1000 transcription upon Gram-positive bacterial infection, while miR-1000 in turn targets the adaptor Myd88 mRNA for degradation. Moreover, we show that upon immune challenge, miR-1000 is significantly induced in the fat body, and fat body-specific manipulations confirm that Dif activates miR-1000 transcription and miR-1000 directly targets Myd88 in this key immune tissue. This dual function of Dif - concurrently inducing immune effectors (e.g., Drosomycin) and their suppressor miR-1000 - establishes a self-limiting circuit: Dif/miR-1000/Myd88 axis. Crucially, miR-1000-mediated suppression of Myd88, the hub of Toll pathway, constrains signal transduction and enables timely termination. Disruption of this axis prolongs Toll pathway activation and compromises host fitness during infection. Furthermore, this miRNA-adaptor regulatory paradigm is evolutionarily conserved, as miRNAs targeting MyD88 (such as miR-155) also inhibit TLR signaling in mammals. Our work reveals a transcriptionally connected feedback mechanism that dynamically restores animal innate immune homeostasis by targeting a central signaling adaptor.

43040328.resumo:
Ceramides are central sphingolipid intermediates whose abundance and molecular composition are closely linked to insulin resistance. Ceramide synthases (CerSs) generate ceramides and, in several family members, also contain a conserved homeodomain with poorly understood metabolic functions. Drosophila has a single CerS, Schlank, which contains a catalytic Lag1p motif and two predicted nuclear localization sequences, NLS1 and NLS2. We investigated how distinct Schlank homeodomain mutations affect high-sugar diet (HSD)-induced insulin resistance.
Endogenous KINLS1 and KIE118A knock-in alleles retained DNA binding and transcriptional repression under basal conditions but increased susceptibility to HSD-induced metabolic dysfunction. Both mutants developed enhanced hyperglycemia and impaired insulin-responsive tGPH recruitment, while KIE118A additionally showed increased FoxO nuclear localization and DILP2 retention in insulin-producing cells. By contrast, fat-body-specific switching to the DNA-binding-deficient NLS2 variant or the catalytically inactive H215D variant attenuated selected HSD-induced phenotypes, including FoxO nuclear accumulation and DILP2 retention, without fully correcting hyperglycemia or reduced body weight. Lipidomic analysis revealed extensive diet-dependent sphingolipid remodeling. In particular, NLS2 and H215D markedly reduced the fat-body ceramide pool, including abundant d14:1/20:0- and d14:1/22:0-containing Cer, CerPE, and HexCer species.
The Schlank homeodomain regulates insulin homeostasis in a site- and tissue-dependent manner. Distinct homeodomain mutations can either increase susceptibility to or partially attenuate HSD-induced insulin resistance, potentially involving insulin signaling, inter-organ communication, and sphingolipid composition.

S17 and Nesterenkonia sp. Act20 and the mesophile Kocuria rosea CH-021. Morphometric responses were assessed using cell surface area and surface-to-volume ratio (S/V), together with SEM image-texture analysis using Haralick-based features. Fixation conditions produced significant strain-dependent differences in both morphometric and image-texture outcomes. The magnitude of morphometric variability differed among strains, and SEM image-texture patterns were not always paralleled by morphometric measurements. These findings indicate that bacterial responses to fixation conditions are strain-dependent and support the combined use of cellular geometry and SEM image-texture descriptors for quantitative comparison of preparation conditions within a standardized SEM workflow.

43046336.resumo:
Genetically engineered crops producing insecticidal Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) proteins are used globally to manage key insect pests, including Helicoverpa zea (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae). In the United States, H. zea has evolved practical resistance to Bt corn and cotton producing crystalline Bt proteins and early warning of resistance to the vegetative insecticidal protein Vip3Aa has been reported. CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing that introduced disruptive mutations in the H. zea chitin synthase 2 (CHS2) gene facilitated creation of a strain (CHS2-KO) with 29 000-fold resistance to Vip3Aa relative to its parental susceptible strain, LAB-S. However, quantitative information about fitness costs associated with CHS2-mediated resistance remains limited. Here, we tested whether CHS2-KO exhibited costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass on diet without Vip3Aa, and examined direct effects on the peritrophic matrix (PM).
Relative to LAB-S, fitness costs in CHS2-KO were 27.8% for neonate to adult survival, 23.2% for neonate to adult development time, and 17.8% for pupal mass. An intact PM was evident in LAB-S and F1 larvae, but not in CHS2-KO larvae.
Mutations disrupting the CHS2 gene in the CHS2-KO strain of H. zea were associated with large fitness costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass when reared on diet under laboratory conditions. Also, no intact PM was evident in CHS2-KO. These results suggest that costs could oppose the spread of knockout alleles in the absence of Vip3Aa, although their magnitude on host plants and applicability to less disruptive CHS2 resistance alleles remain to be determined. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry. 43044582.resumo: The ability of vertebrates to conquer land is attributed to innovations in respiration and locomotion. However, land adaptation profoundly reshaped mucosal surfaces such as the skin, the main interface between hosts and the environment. To adapt to land, African lungfish annually remodel their skin, forming a cocoon. Here, we report the discovery of a small pore-forming toxin in African lungfish, Protop-CrTX-A, with no other vertebrate counterpart that is sufficient to drive epithelial morphogenesis transcriptional programs. In free-swimming lungfish, goblet cells secrete Protop-CrTX-A into the mucus. During estivation, this niche is replaced by a mucin-low/basal epithelial niche, adjacent to a granulocyte immune niche that becomes the predominant source of Protop-CrTX-A in the estivated skin. Protop-CrTX-A acts as a reversible switch for skin remodeling, sufficient to convert African lungfish skin between aquatic and terrestrial states. We propose that innate immunity, through its capacity to remodel tissues, was a key driver of vertebrate water-land transitions.

43038963.resumo: Maternally inherited, intracellular bacteria of the genus Wolbachia are extremely widespread among arthropods. Their evolutionary success is owed to frequent host shifts and rapid subsequent spread within host populations, often facilitated by Wolbachia-induced reproductive manipulations. Theory suggests that often, Wolbachia spread may also be explained by fitness benefits, the nature of which have remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that Wolbachia's success in many solitary bee species is strongly associated with the presence of a gene cassette enabling Wolbachia to synthesize biotin (vitamin B7). This ability is absent from almost all other Wolbachia strains but common among bee-associated strains. We show that Wolbachia occurs in up to 60% of all bee species and that strains carrying this rare genomic element have independently spread into numerous bee hosts recently. We further demonstrate that the presence of the biotin operon is associated with specialized diets in several bee species, suggesting a previously overlooked nutritional role of Wolbachia in this group of important pollinators. Overall, our results suggest that nutritional benefits provided by symbionts may represent a more widespread and important mechanism by which reproductive manipulators spread into new host species than previously appreciated.

This review synthesizes current knowledge on the immunopathogenesis of FL, emphasizing the roles of chronic inflammation, genetics, immune dysregulation, microbial translocation, and lymphatic adipose tissue remodeling in disease persistence. We highlight emerging diagnostic biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and integrative management strategies, and outline critical gaps that hinder effective morbidity reduction. Advancing stage-specific diagnostic approaches and exploring intervention mechanisms will be essential to improve quality of life for affected individuals and achieve meaningful, sustainable elimination of lymphatic filariasis-associated morbidity.

GPX4 deletion markedly increased susceptibility to CS-induced cell death and was not rescued by ferrostatin-1. The persistence of drug-resistant epilepsy highlights the need for new therapies that target novel mechanisms while maintaining synaptic strength and minimizing side effects. Small molecules of natural origin with anti-epileptogenic potential can influence altered synaptic deficits and reducing seizure threshold, offering a strategy to restore cellular energy homeostasis and slow the progression of epilepsy and associated comorbidities.
We used a combination of approaches including behavioural assays, immunostaining and electrophysiological recordings to study the synaptic contributions to reduced seizure-threshold in both Drosophila and mouse models of epilepsy. In addition, we used affinity-purification with synthesized beads specific for our small molecule to identify its cellular partners.
We found that administration of Urolithin-A (UA), a small molecule of natural origin, mitigated behavioural and synaptic dysfunctions under chemically and genetically induced epileptic conditions in Drosophila. Additionally, chronic treatment with UA attenuated the altered single-cell and network synaptic transmission in PTZ-induced chronic kindling of mice. However, UA exerted no seizure-suppressive effects in in vitro epileptic conditions, suggesting the absence of acute anti-epileptic effects. In addition, we identified the direct interactor of UA as the complex of tubulin dimer and VDAC1. Molecular docking analyses also predicted that urolithin A interacts with VDAC1. Consistent with the neuroprotective role of VDAC1 downregulation reported in previous studies, neuron-specific knockdown of VDAC1 in Drosophila phenocopied the effects of UA.
Collectively, our data show that UA exerts disease-modifying anti-epileptic effects in both Drosophila and mouse models with VDAC1 identified as a critical functional mediator; however, direct functional modulation of VDAC1 and associated partners by UA will require further experimental validation. These findings provide the blueprint for future drug discovery targeting VDAC1-dependent pathways.

U87 GBM cells were treated with TMZ and fractionated RT, with or without transient chlorogenic acid (CGA) exposure administered prior to irradiation. Transient CGA exposure significantly potentiated TMZ + RT cytotoxicity, increasing membrane damage and reducing cell survival after irradiation. CGA induced an early increase in oxidative stress followed by delayed depletion of reduced NADPH and GSH, amplifying redox imbalance under combinedchemoradiotherapy. Metabolic analyses indicated enhanced glycolytic engagement without further stimulation of mitochondrial respiration.
ER-associated NADPH metabolism represents a clinically relevant determinant of redox resilience in GBM, with H6PD emerging as an independent prognostic marker within this metabolic axis. In a U87 proof-of-concept model, transient, timing-based metabolic priming with CGA disrupts antioxidant buffering and amplifies oxidative vulnerability during chemoradiotherapy, thereby enhancing tumor in vitro. These findings provide a strong mechanistic and translational rationale for targeting ER-linked redox metabolism as an adjuvant strategy to improve GBM responsiveness to standard chemoradiotherapy.

43037123.resumo: Regeneration is a coordinated process that restores tissue integrity following damage. Following injury, tissues initiate early responses, including epithelial remodeling and clearance of cellular debris. However, how debris clearance is coordinated with regenerative growth to ensure efficient tissue repair remains poorly understood. To address how early damage responses, particularly debris clearance, are coordinated with regeneration, we used a genetic ablation system in Drosophila wing imaginal discs to induce apoptosis in the pouch region. Targeted damage generates cellular debris that localizes to both the apical and basal sides of the epithelium. We show that most cellular debris is cleared within two days after damage, although some debris persists apical to the regenerating epithelium. Our data indicate that residual debris consists of a heterogeneous mixture of cellular components, suggesting no preferential targeting by the clearance machinery. Notably, immune cells are not recruited to the damaged tissue due to restricted access by an intact basement membrane. Instead, we discovered that debris clearance is mediated by efferocytosis, whereby neighboring hinge epithelial cells activate JNK signaling and engulf debris via lysosomal formation. Reduction of efferocytosis by mutation of the phagocytic receptor Draper delays debris removal and increases debris persistence. This impairment has a modest impact on regeneration, as measured by adult wing size. Together, our results reveal a previously unappreciated role for epithelial cells as non-professional phagocytes for debris clearance during regeneration.

ensaio.historia:
Durante quase um século, a parasitologia molecular operou sob um dogma redutor: para entender por que um mosquito transmite ou bloqueia a malária, ou por que o camundongo desenvolve edema cerebral, deveríamos buscar sempre "o gene" ou "a citocina". Mapeamos vias inteiras (Toll, Imd, JAK-STAT), sequenciamos transcriptomas de células únicas e quantificamos centenas de RNAs mensageiros.

No entanto, uma pergunta desconfortável permaneceu sem resposta na bancada: **como decisões vitais de infecção ocorrem em frações de segundo, muito antes de qualquer RNA polimerase conseguir transcrever um gene?**

Quando o oocineto atinge o microvilo do mosquito, a digestão do sangue está no auge. Milhões de eritrócitos se rompem, gerando uma pressão coloidosmótica massiva, liberação letal de hemo livre e fluxo turbulento não-newtoniano. O parasito não tem horas para esperar uma via gênica ser ativada. Ele precisa explorar as propriedades biofísicas nativas do epitélio: diferenças de potencial elétrico entre células vizinhas, zonas de menor tensão mecânica e condensação líquida de proteínas de superfície.

Se quisermos descobrir o que não sabemos que existe, precisamos sair da nossa própria vizinhança conceitual. É no cruzamento com a biologia de sistemas de organelas, com a bioeletricidade do desenvolvimento e com a física da matéria mole que residem as próximas grandes viradas da nossa bancada.

grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Maya Schuldiner revolucionou a biologia celular ao quebrar o paradigma de que as organelas intracelulares se comunicavam exclusivamente através de vesículas secretoras (via clássica de Golgi e retículo).

Usando triagem robótica em larga escala de leveduras (SGA - Synthetic Genetic Array) combinada com microscopia de fluorescência de altíssima resolução, seu laboratório no Weizmann descobriu que organelas como retículo endoplasmático, mitocôndrias, peroxissomos, gotas lipídicas e vacúolos estão fisicamente conectadas por pontes proteicas especializadas ("tethers"), formando uma malha contínua chamada de 'contactoma'. Essas fendas de 10 a 30 nanômetros permitem o transporte ultrarrápido de lipídios, íons cálcio e intermediários metabólicos vitais, operando como cabos de alta velocidade dentro da célula.

grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Michael Levin é pioneiro na redefinição da biologia do desenvolvimento e regeneração: enquanto a maioria dos biólogos encara eletricidade celular como algo restrito a neurônios e músculos, Levin provou que **todas as células vivas mantêm gradientes bioelétricos de membrana (Vmem)** e se comunicam através de junções comunicantes (gap junctions).

temas_expansao.tema: Contactoma de Organelas & Homeostase de Hemo no Inseto
temas_expansao.o_que_e: Como os sítios de contato membrana-membrana desviam a toxicidade do hemo livre no intestino de mosquitos hematófagos durante o repasto sanguíneo.

temas_expansao.contexto:
Durante a digestão da hemoglobina, a concentração de hemo livre no intestino médio atinge níveis milimolares letais. Sabíamos que os mosquitos contam com agregação de hemo em hemozoína e proteção por antioxidantes.

Contudo, a física dos sítios de contato de membranas (MCS) revela que o trânsito intracelular de lipídios e metabólitos oxidáveis é protegido por canais fechados entre o retículo endoplasmático e as organelas de estoque. Mapear o contactoma intestinal em resposta ao repasto normal vs dieta hiperlipídica/hiperglicêmica (HFHS) abre uma frente experimental completamente nova para o LUCHM.

temas_expansao.tema: Bioeletricidade de Epitélios & Permissividade de Barreira
temas_expansao.o_que_e: Como os gradientes elétricos trans-epiteliais e potenciais de membrana mantêm a ancoragem das junções oclusivas antes de danos estruturais.
temas_expansao.pergunta_provocativa: A permeabilidade da barreira hematoencefálica e da membrana peritrófica é controlada por campos bioelétricos antes de alterações estruturais?
temas_expansao.contexto:
O rompimento de junções oclusivas (claudina-5, occludina) tem sido estudado sob a ótica proteica e transcricional. No entanto, pesquisas bioelétricas comprovam que o potencial elétrico trans-epitelial mantém as moléculas de adesão sob tensão mecânica contínua.

Quando ocorre estresse oxidativo ou agressão por citocinas, a despolarização iônica precoce relaxa a força de ancoragem das claudinas, permitindo a passagem de fluidos e patógenos antes de qualquer degradação proteolítica visível.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Espectroscopia AFM-IR em Nanoescala (Photo-Thermal Induced Resonance)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Combinação de Microscopia de Força Atômica com Espectroscopia de Infravermelho (AFM-IR), permitindo caracterização química de espécies moleculares com resolução espacial de 10 a 20 nanômetros.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Durante décadas, a espectroscopia de infravermelho clássica (FTIR) foi limitada pelo limite de difração da luz óptica (~2 a 10 micrômetros), sendo incapaz de identificar compostos químicos dentro de organelas isoladas.

O desenvolvimento do AFM-IR contornou esse limite físico ao utilizar a ponta ultrafina de um microscópio de força atômica para detectar a expansão térmica nanomecânica da amostra quando excitada por um laser infravermelho pulsado e sintonizável. Com isso, tornou-se possível obter o espectro de absorção química exato de nanodomínios lipídicos, agregados amiloides e depósitos minerais sem marcadores fluorescentes.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Optogenética Não-Invasiva em Insetos Vivos (Canais CsChrimson)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Controle óptico remoto de neurônios, enterócitos e células musculares em mosquitos livres e intactos, usando luz vermelha profunda (CsChrimson) que penetra a cutícula sem lesão térmica.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Por décadas, testar a função de um circuito neuropeptídico ou da motilidade intestinal de um mosquito exigia dissecção traumática, microinjeção de drogas ou silenciamento por RNAi sistêmico (que afeta o inseto por dias).

A criação de canais de rodopsina de canal ativados por luz vermelha (CsChrimson, desenvolvidos por Boyden, Levin e colaboradores) permitiu que pesquisadores ativem subpopulações neurais e células enteroendócrinas específicas com um simples flash de LED vermelho enquanto o inseto voa ou se alimenta em tempo real, sem qualquer agulha ou anestesia.
